transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yeah. So, my supervisor basically told me I had to come see someone. What brought me in is I keep leaving my station on the floor, or like, popping up and walking around during our shift meetings when I'm supposed to stay put. He says it's becoming a real safety problem because I just take off before I even think about it. 

But honestly, standing at the line is just... well, we make these plastic moldings for car doors, and it gets so repetitive. Plus, the floor is solid concrete, so I bought these new steel-toe boots from Walmart last weekend because my old ones were totally worn through on the heel. But the new ones have this crazy squeak. Like, every time I walk down the aisle, it's just squeak, squeak, squeak. My friend Sarah—she works over in the packing department—she told me she can hear me coming from all the way across the warehouse. We usually go to lunch together, but the vending machine in the breakroom has been broken for like three weeks, and it just eats your quarters if you try to get a soda, which is super annoying because who even carries exact change anymore? 

Um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, yeah. My supervisor. He's just really on my case about leaving my spot without asking.
Do you find it hard to stay in one place for long, like an urge to move or feeling restless, even when you know you should stay put?

Yeah, exactly! It's like... when I'm trying to just stand still by the molding machine, or like when we have those safety trainings where we have to sit in those awful folding chairs, it feels like this pressure is just building up inside my whole body. And I just have to move, or pace, or stretch, or go do something right then. It's impossible. 

Speaking of those folding chairs, they are the absolute worst. They're metal and freezing cold, and one time, I swear, I almost pinched my finger in the hinge trying to set it up. My uncle had these chairs just like them at his house for his Fourth of July barbecue last year. We had so much food—brisket, ribs, potato salad... Oh, my aunt makes the best potato salad, she puts a little bit of mustard in it, which sounds weird but it's actually amazing. She brought it in this huge yellow bowl that used to belong to my grandma. Grandma had this whole set of vintage Pyrex, the ones with the little flowers on them? I think they're worth a lot of money now. I saw someone selling a set on Facebook Marketplace for like, two hundred dollars. Can you believe that? Two hundred dollars for bowls! 

Anyway, um... yeah, so standing still or sitting just feels like I'm gonna explode if I don't move.
Do you find it hard to focus on tasks or stay organized, like losing track of what you're doing or getting distracted easily?

Yeah, I mean, definitely. Like, when they make me do the inventory logs at the end of the shift, or right now I'm supposed to be reading these training pages for the new CNC machine... I start out really trying, I swear. But after just a few minutes, the numbers or the words, they just start blurring together. I end up having to go back and read the same paragraph over and over because I didn't actually take any of it in. 

Which is so frustrating, because the CNC machine is actually pretty cool. It's this huge, loud thing that cuts the plastic, and the guy who installed it—Dave, I think his name was—he had this crazy tattoo of a dragon on his arm. It went all the way from his wrist up to his shoulder, and it had these bright red scales. I always wanted a tattoo, maybe like a little butterfly or a star right here on my ankle. My mom hates tattoos, though. She says they look unprofessional, but honestly, half the people at the warehouse have them. Even the shift manager has one on his neck. It's like a barcode or something. I don't know why you'd want a barcode on your neck, it reminds me of scanning groceries. 

I used to work at a grocery store, actually, bagging groceries, but I got fired because I kept putting the bread at the bottom of the bags by accident. People get so mad about squished bread. I mean, it still tastes the same, right? But whatever. 

So, um, wait. What were we talking about? Oh, right, the training pages. Yeah, I just can't keep my focus on them at all.
When you were a kid, did you also have trouble sitting still, focusing, or staying organized with your schoolwork or other tasks?

Oh, yeah, totally. It's not just a new thing. Even back in elementary school, I was always that kid. Like, I just could not stay in my seat to save my life. I was always talking over the teacher, getting in trouble for blurting out answers before she even finished asking the question, or just wandering around the classroom when we were supposed to be doing silent reading. My mom got so many notes sent home about it. 

I remember one time in third grade, Mrs. Gable—she was my teacher, she always wore these really bright, chunky necklaces, like big plastic beads in neon colors. I don't know where she bought them, probably some craft fair or something. My aunt loves craft fairs. She makes these little soaps shaped like seashells and sells them at the farmers market on weekends. They smell like lavender and peppermint, which is a really weird combination if you think about it, but people buy them like crazy. She tried to teach me how to make them once, but you have to wait for the soap base to melt in this double boiler thing, and it takes forever. I kept trying to stir it too fast and splashed hot soap all over the counter. It was a huge mess. It took us like two hours to scrape it all off the linoleum. 

Linoleum is the worst floor to clean, honestly. It always looks dirty even when you just mopped it. 

But, um... yeah, so school was always like that. Me wandering around, talking too much, getting notes sent home. It's basically always been this way.
